entries.term: Assembly of the wicked / synagogue of Satan
entries.definition: A counterfeit congregation claiming covenant standing while gathered against the covenant's Lord. Korah's company; the brood of vipers and children of the Devil, the father of lies; the assembly surrounding the Messiah; and those who say they are Jews but are not display the pattern. This is a spiritual identity defined by allegiance and rejection of Messiah, never by ancestry.
entries.citations: (Ps 22:16; Num 14:35; 16:3; Matt 3:7; 12:34; John 8:44; Acts 4:27; Rev 2:9; 3:9) · see What Is the Point?, ch. 25

entries.definition: The curse-ground's fruitless growth — worldly care and deceitful riches that choke the word, offer false protection, and end in fire.
entries.citations: (Gen 3:18; Matt 13:22; Judg 9:15; 2 Sam 23:6-7; Heb 6:8) · see The Parables of the Kingdom, ch. 2

entries.definition:
Where beginnings and returns come from — the front. Hebrew qedem joins “east” with “before” and “ancient”: Eden is planted eastward; the sanctuary's front door is its east gate; God's glory returns through that gate; and Christ's coming moves from east to west. The compass direction is the literal image beneath the symbol.
[.opposite]Opposite: West.
entries.citations: (Gen 2:8; Ex 27:13-16; Ezek 43:1-4; 46:1-3; Matt 24:27) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35

entries.definition: Leaders and representatives of the assemblies, seated as a court around the throne — the constellations among the host of heaven and their stars.
entries.citations: (1 Kgs 22:19; Isa 24:23; Rev 4:4; Matt 19:28; Ps 89:5-7) · see Sun, Moon & Stars, ch. 29

entries.definition: The scattered firstborn whose seed becomes the fulness of the nations.
entries.citations: (Gen 48:19) · see Jacob, Israel & Ephraim, ch. 45

entries.definition: The lamp of the body, revealing the light within. A good eye gives; an evil eye withholds; God's fiery eyes — His righteous watchers — range throughout the earth and shine like the stars in heaven.
entries.citations: (Matt 6:22-23; Prov 22:9; 23:6; Zech 4:10; Rev 1:14; 5:6) · see Sun, Moon & Stars, ch. 29

entries.definition:
One who hears God's word and will not do it — the lawless, not the unintelligent.
[.opposite]Opposite: Wise.
entries.citations: (Ps 14:1; Matt 7:26) · see The Fool and the Wise, ch. 20

entries.definition: The rage of the wicked at the righteous, especially when they see the kingdom from which they are excluded. Their grief, hatred, gnashing, and destruction follow the pattern of the Psalms and Stephen's accusers.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: the anguish of the damned under conscious, everlasting torment.
entries.citations: (Ps 112:10; Ps 37:12; Luke 13:28; Acts 7:54; Matt 8:12) · see The Weeping and the Gnashing | (Ps 112:10; Ps 37:12; Luke 13:28; Acts 7:54; Matt 8:12) · see The Weeping and the Gnashing, in the free digital edition at TimeTested.Bible

entries.definition: The scattered house of Israel mingled with the nations, sought and regathered; more generally, any unrepentant sinner.
entries.citations: (Matt 15:24) · see Jacob, Israel & Ephraim, ch. 45

entries.definition: The covenant identity of a house, consisting of its Head's Word, covenant law, and fruitful priesthood. Substituting any one creates a counterfeit Name; rejecting, replacing, or removing any one takes the Name in vain.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: the person's character, authority, and reputation.

entries.definition:
The absence of Day and Light — visible obedience — marked by sleep or death and by sinful deeds concealed in darkness. At the largest scale, it is the period from the fall of man until the Kingdom of God begins on earth.
[.opposite]Opposite: Day.
entries.citations: (Gen 1:5; 1 Thess 5:5-7) · see Light and Darkness, ch. 21

entries.definition: A great city of the sea — Gentile people who repent and rise in judgment against those who reject Jesus.
entries.citations: (Matt 12:41) · see The Sign of Jonah, ch. 4

entries.definition: Covenant blood displayed outwardly — and counterfeited by those who wear the form without the substance.
entries.citations: (Isa 1:18; Josh 2:18; Heb 9:19; Rev 17:4) · see Garments & Armor, ch. 43 — derived in the digital edition’s symbol study at TimeTested.Bible

entries.definition: A generative word or life planted to reproduce after its kind. In the sower it is God's word; in the wheat and tares it is children; the promised Seed is Messiah; and one planted person may grow into a house, people, or nation-tree.
entries.citations: (Gen 1:11-12; 3:15; Isa 51:2; Matt 13:19, 31-32, 38; John 12:24; Gal 3:16) · see The Parables of the Kingdom, ch. 2, Trees, ch. 41, and Grass, ch. 42

entries.definition:
The symbolic Way and pattern of the world shaped like Death's substance: sin, darkness, and bondage whose wages end at the pit or grave. Opposite the shadow of Christ—the appointed times, assemblies, and humbled Way shaped like His substance—which leads through death to the gift of eternal life.
[.opposite]Opposite: the Shadow of Christ.
entries.citations: (Ps 23:4; 107:10, 14; Isa 9:2; Luke 1:78-79; Rom 6:23; Phil 2:5-9) · see Shadow, ch. 17, and Heaven and Hell, ch. 16

entries.definition:
The transgression of the law — Scripture's own definition: “sin is the transgression of the law”; where no law is, there is no transgression, and by the law is the knowledge of sin.
[.opposite]Opposite: Righteousness.
entries.citations: (1 John 3:4; Rom 4:15; 3:20; 7:7) · see Grace, Mercy & the Gift, ch. 24

entries.definition: The righteous, who rule the night with the Son — “they that be wise shall shine… as the stars for ever”; the twelve stars are the twelve tribes, gathered into the twelve constellations, the Mazzaroth.
entries.citations: (Dan 12:3; Ps 136:9; Gen 37:9; Rev 12:1; Job 38:32) · see Sun, Moon & Stars, ch. 29

entries.definition: The nations in turmoil — the raging sea, stilled at Christ's word, “Peace, be still”.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: divine judgment, and the trials of life which Christ has power to calm.
entries.citations: (Ps 65:7; Isa 17:12-13; Mark 4:39; Luke 21:25) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40

entries.definition: The prophet that teacheth lies — Isaiah's own decode, with head and tail already defined by the covenant: obedience makes Israel “the head, and not the tail,” and the curse inverts it. The dragon fells a third of the stars with its tail — the led destroyed by the misleading — and the trumpet armies' serpent-tails “had heads”: the liar enthroned. Moses is told to seize the serpent exactly there.
entries.citations: (Isa 9:15-16; Deut 28:13, 44; Rev 12:4; 9:19; Ex 4:4) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35

entries.definition: The words of the one who speaks; the Shepherd's voice is His words.
entries.citations: (John 10:27) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6

entries.definition: Salvation — the covenant's enclosure: “thou shalt call thy walls Salvation”; God Himself “a wall of fire round about.” The counterfeit is self-built — wealth's high wall “in his own conceit,” and the whitewashed wall of false peace that the storm flattens.
entries.citations: (Isa 60:18; Zech 2:5; Prov 18:11; Ezek 13:10-15) · see The Parable of the Vineyard | (Isa 60:18; Zech 2:5; Prov 18:11; Ezek 13:10-15) · see The Parable of the Vineyard, in the free digital edition at TimeTested.Bible
